newsitem.title: UK: London freight market seen as generally dull.
newsitem.headline: London freight market seen as generally dull.

text.p: Brokers described the market as generally dull, with some holding the view that this would persist over the forthcoming holiday period.
However, conditions for panamaxes in the East and for handymaxes in the Atlantic were reckoned to be especially firm.

The turnover in reported grain fixtures was low and concern was expressed about problems in Taiwan restricting imports, nonetheless though, demand for tonnage from grain houses continued strong from Argentina and Brazil.
The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) posted a gain of eleven points to 1,526.

GRAIN - Cargill nominated their own tonnage for an early April 54,000 tonnes heavy grain stem U.S. Gulf/Japan and covered U.S. Gulf/Continent on private terms (there was some doubt about whether or not it was a panamax or another size involved).
Cargill still have a panamax requirement for mid April for Nopac/Japan (ideas only $14.75 basis no combo).
Continental booked Gulluk 60,000 dwt for 2,821,000 cubic feet grain for a prompt shipment of corn and meals U.S. Gulf/Jeddah and Dammam for a lumpsum close to $1.32 million basis two discharge ports.
There was little news of fixtures from EC south America.
There was talk that Tradigrain and/or Shipmair had booked panamaxes to the Far East, and that Sonic Youth 61,569 dwt had been fixed from the area, but details were scarce.
Brokers again underlined the healthy level of demand for handies from South America but actual details of fixtures were being withheld.
Cargill was thought to be trading closely a parcel of 25,000 tonnes maize Ilheus/Continent for March/April loading at about $21.00.
New enquiry from grain charterers saw Glencore with 50,000 tonnes wheat Dunkirk/Aqaba for prompt shipment.

Others included 25,000 barley Finland/Tunisia for early April, HMM for a vessel on timecharter to load 35,000 tonnes corn delivery U.S. Gulf April 6/15 trip Singapore-Japan range, and Soufflet with 30,000 tonnes wheat Columbia River/Hodeidah April 7/12.

The Australian Wheat Board added to already ample demand for panamax tonnage in the East, with requirements for tonnage for monthly shipments of 50,000 wheat from Australia to Egypt for April, May and June.
The BIFFEX futures closed 15 to 51 points down on 154 lots. Most active April on 82 lots, traded last at 1,589, down 51.

MINERALS - In a quiet sector, Rohstoffhandel was reported to have taken Sishen 170,000 dwt for another consecutive iron ore cargo from Port Cartier or Seven Islands to Rotterdam, and Silvergate was fixed for a prompt 100,000/10 iron ore Narvik/Dunkirk east by Sideco on private terms.
HANDYSIZES - Pressure from the Plate and Brazil has pushed rates upwards for handymaxes, but details are being kept private.
In the East, Fassa 37,994 dwt was believed to have been relet by South Korean charterers for four to six months at close to $8,600 daily.
San Pietro 46,606 dwt was thought to have been fixed west coast India/Whampoa at over $10,000 daily.
The Morning Sky 45,000 dwt was reported booked for a Pacific round voyage at $9,500 daily, and Nena F 42,263 dwt went for a Port Hedland round voyage at the same rate, both to Hanjin.
